newsitem.title: UK: Halifax shares firm, reach post-launch high.
newsitem.headline: Halifax shares firm, reach post-launch high.

text.p: Shares in Halifax Plc gained seven pence to 756p at 0845 GMT on Tuesday, the highest level since the newly created bank's market debut on June 2 and compared with the 776p peak achieved on that day.
The rise was made on volume of almost four million shares and followed a 13.5p rally on Monday.
Halifax's progress was amid a rather mixed financial sector, with National Westminster Bank Plc retreating 19p to 796p after strong gains on Monday.
Rumours of a merger with Abbey National Plc had lifted Natwest 35.5p to 816p -- a rise of 4.5 percent -- but the rally soon petered out.
Sentiment may be further clouded by press comment that Natwest's apparent enthusiasm for a merger displays a lack of confidence in its own strategic vision.
Natwest's recent rally follows persistent weakness as investors signal their doubts over the group's prospects.

Since last June it has underperformed U.K. peers by 30 percent, lagging arch rival Barclays Plc by 23 percent and the Abbey by 27 percent, according to a relative performance study conducted on Reuters 3000.
